questions.stem: MR Spectroscopy of a brain lesion shows markedly elevated Choline peak, decreased N-acetylaspartate (NAA) peak, and presence of a Lactate peak. Which type of pathology is most suggested by this spectral pattern?
questions.stemHtml: MR Spectroscopy of a brain lesion shows markedly elevated Choline peak, decreased N-acetylaspartate (NAA) peak, and presence of a Lactate peak. Which type of pathology is most suggested by this spectral pattern?
questions.solution: ation: MR Spectroscopy provides information about the biochemical composition of brain tissue. Elevated Choline (Cho) reflects increased cell membrane turnover, typically seen in tumors. Decreased N-acetylaspartate (NAA) indicates neuronal loss or dysfunction. Presence of Lactate suggests anaerobic metabolism, which can occur in high-grade tumors, infarcts, or abscesses. However, the combination of markedly elevated Cho, decreased NAA, and often a lactate peak (and sometimes lipid peaks indicating necrosis) is most characteristic of a high-grade neoplasm like glioblastoma. Acute infarcts show prominent lactate and rapidly falling NAA, but Cho is usually not markedly elevated initially. Abscesses often show lactate and amino acid peaks. Demyelinating lesions may show decreased NAA and sometimes elevated Cho, but usually not as marked as in high-grade tumors, and lactate is less common. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.solution: lass="customMeta" data-dictid="b5d5db1f591692777190869c6a7223">Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (JME) is a common idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndrome typically starting in adolescence. It is characterized by a triad of seizure types: myoclonic jerks (often in the morning), generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS), and sometimes absence seizures. A key diagnostic feature is the EEG pattern showing generalized spike-wave or polyspike-wave discharges, often faster than 3 Hz (typically 4-6 Hz, though 3 Hz can occur), frequently provoked by photic stimulation or sleep deprivation. While CAE also shows 3-Hz spike-wave discharges, it typically presents earlier in childhood with absence seizures as the predominant type, and GTCS are less common. Temporal lobe epilepsy is focal.
